spatial_claims.claim: AD is a segment with annex DG; points A, D, G are collinear with D between A and G (AD = AG - GD)
Squares on AG and DG are applied to rational line AC, producing breadths AH and KH along AC
DG is bisected at E; point E is midpoint of segment DG, collinear with A, D, G
Point H on segment AG such that AH * HG = sq(EG) = sq(DG)/4, obtained by applying parallelogram to AG deficient by a square
Lines o, p constructed abstractly via sq(o) = AC * AN, sq(p) = AC * HG
w = o - p with sq(w) = AC * AD, confirmed by algebraic identity 2.7

configuration_map: All geometric elements are collinear points on a single line (A, D, E, G, H) plus rectangular area applications to a perpendicular rational line AC. E is the midpoint of DG. H is a point on AG determined by the area equation AH * HG = sq(DG/2). The lines o, p, w are abstract magnitudes defined by area equations, not geometric configurations. The entire proof operates through commensurability relations and algebraic identities with no complex spatial configuration.
skip_reason: This is a Book 10 proposition about irrational lines (third apotome and second apotome of a medial). The proof is purely algebraic/proportional, dealing entirely with commensurability and incommensurability of magnitudes, medial areas, and algebraic identities (II.5, II.7). The only geometric elements are collinear points on a line and standard area applications, with no angles, triangles, circles, interior/exterior claims, or ray orderings that could produce spatial configuration contradictions.
